item.title: Canadian Tire ordered to pay nearly $1.3 million for false advertising
item.description: Canadian Tire has been ordered to pay just under $1.3 million after pleading guilty to 74 counts of violating sections of Quebec’s Consumer Protection Act related to false advertising. Crown prosecutor Jérôme Dussault says the Canadian retail giant agreed to the settlement after initially pleading not guilty. At the Montreal courthouse, Quebec court Judge Simon […]

item.title: Skiing’s regulatory body rejects ‘wild rumor’ ski jumpers are enhancing anatomy to gain distance
item.description: PREDAZZO, Italy (AP) — The regulatory body for skiing on Friday dismissed as a “wild rumor” reports that ski jumpers are enhancing their groin area to gain distance as the Winter Olympics begins. A report by the German tabloid Bild last month suggested some ski jumpers were injecting hyaluronic acid in their genitals or wearing a condom-like […]

item.title: Overnight train derailment in Surrey results in coal spill
item.description: A train derailment in Surrey overnight resulted in coal being spilled on the rails and nearby, Surrey Fire Service says.

item.title: Pipeline protest created safety risks, but journalists were let in, says RCMP officer
item.description: The senior RCMP officer co-ordinating enforcement at a British Columbia pipeline protest in 2021 says journalists were permitted to go through an "access control point" set up by police, and anyone who claimed to be media was allowed in.

item.title: VPD arrests four suspects in North Vancouver home invasion
item.description: After a 45-year-old man was held hostage inside a home in North Vancouver, the Vancouver Police Department (VPD) says it has made an arrest of four suspects.

item.title: B.C. asks top court to hear DRIPA appeal, saying ‘core democratic values’ at stake
item.description: British Columbia has applied to the Supreme Court of Canada to hear an appeal against a landmark court ruling that found the province's mineral claims regime was “inconsistent" with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, embodied in a provincial law known as DRIPA.

item.title: CKWX celebrates 30 years of all news radio
item.description: It was 30 years ago this Sunday that Vancouver was introduced to a new radio service.

item.title: Surrey police start video campaign to dissuade people from getting involved in extortion crimes
item.description: The Surrey Police Service (SPS) says it has published a series of videos on social media aiming to reach people who are being lured into committing extortion-related crimes.

item.title: Mild weather in Metro Vancouver will not last into weekend
item.description: The stretch of mild weather in the Lower Mainland is coming to an end and will stop before the weekend starts.

item.title: Police stop Lamborghini driver going double the speed limit on Alex Fraser Bridge
item.description: A Lamborghini SUV driver had to give up his car keys after police caught the vehicle going more than double the allowed speed on the Alex Fraser Bridge.
